sources_notes.space_weather.csv: NASA DONKI (CCMC space weather database), 2025-06-01 to 2025-12-31. mars_impact comes from DONKI's own model runs and instrument lists.
sources_notes.radiation.csv: ESTIMATE, not a measurement at this site: Curiosity RAD surface average at Gale, 0.64 mSv/day (Hassler et al. 2014, Science 343). Applied unchanged at Jezero, which sits about 2 km higher than Gale crater's floor under a thinner atmosphere, so the real dose is probably somewhat higher.
sources_notes.dem.tif: HiRISE (MRO), USGS Mars 2020 TRN mosaic of Jezero: JEZ_hirise_soc_006_DTM_MOLAtopography_DeltaGeoid_1m_Eqc_latTs0_lon0_blend40.tif
sources_notes.weather.csv: MEDA (Perseverance): 2 file(s), sols 420-420, hourly means of air temperature and pressure. dust_tau is an estimate (0.6), not a MEDA measurement.
sources_notes.relief.png: Derived from HiRISE (MRO), USGS Mars 2020 TRN mosaic of Jezero: JEZ_hirise_soc_006_DTM_MOLAtopography_DeltaGeoid_1m_Eqc_latTs0_lon0_blend40.tif: hillshade, sun azimuth 315°, altitude 45°. Built 2026-11-14 by terrain/hazards.py. Confidence: high (direct from the DTM).
sources_notes.slope.png: Derived from HiRISE (MRO), USGS Mars 2020 TRN mosaic of Jezero: JEZ_hirise_soc_006_DTM_MOLAtopography_DeltaGeoid_1m_Eqc_latTs0_lon0_blend40.tif: slope in degrees (central differences on the 5 m grid). Built 2026-11-14 by terrain/hazards.py. Confidence: high at 5 m scale; slopes shorter than one cell (5 m) are smoothed out.
sources_notes.hazard.tif: Derived from HiRISE (MRO) slope and roughness and THEMIS (Mars Odyssey) thermal inertia, thresholds in terrain/thresholds.toml. Built 2026-11-14 by terrain/hazards.py. Careful over 10°, no-go over 20° (cliffs included); roughness over 0.5 / 1.0 m RMS from a local plane (3 x 3 cells); thermal inertia under 250 / 150 SI (THEMIS 100 m pixels, coarse); cells without height data are no-go. Confidence: medium. The thresholds are starting values, and boulders smaller than the 5 m grid are not visible.
sources_notes.shelter_time.png: Derived from the routing model (routing/plan_route.py) on the HiRISE (MRO) terrain model and the real hazard map. Built 2026-11-14. Minutes back to the rover from every cell, walking model and limits in routing/config.toml. Confidence: medium (walking speed and limits are scenario assumptions).
sources_notes.route.geojson: Calculated 2026-11-14 by routing/plan_route.py (balanced profile) on the real hazard map and HiRISE terrain. Confidence: medium (same assumptions as plan.json).
sources_notes.plan.json: Calculated 2026-11-14 by routing/plan_route.py. Times use the walking model in routing/config.toml (scenario values); dose uses the radiation.csv estimate.
sources_notes.waypoints.geojson: Stop positions chosen 2026-11-14 from our real layers: CRISM (MRO) minerals, THEMIS (Mars Odyssey) thermal inertia and the HiRISE-derived hazard map. Confidence: medium (CRISM thresholds are relative, tuned by eye; minerals.png keeps only pass/fail, not strength).
sources_notes.crater/dem.tif: USGS Mars 2020 CTX DEM mosaic, 20 m: M20_JezeroCrater_CTXDEM_20m.tif, resampled to 40 m cells (average of the 20 m pixels). Built 2026-11-14. Confidence: medium for broad terrain (crater walls, scarps, the delta front); low for anything smaller than a few cells. Slopes are averaged over 40 m, so they read lower than the 5 m site slopes, and boulders and small ledges do not show.
sources_notes.crater/hazard.tif: Derived from USGS Mars 2020 CTX DEM mosaic, 20 m (M20_JezeroCrater_CTXDEM_20m.tif): slope only, rover-scale, 40 m from CTX DEM, misses boulders/small ledges. Built 2026-11-14. Confidence: medium for broad terrain (crater walls, scarps, the delta front); low for anything smaller than a few cells. Slopes are averaged over 40 m, so they read lower than the 5 m site slopes, and boulders and small ledges do not show.
sources_notes.photos.geojson: NASA Mars 2020 raw images (mars.nasa.gov/mars2020/multimedia/raw-images, JSON API), 15 Navcam and Mastcam-Z full frames taken at eye level (mast about 2 m up) inside or near our site, sols 408-731. Positions from NASA/JPL's published Perseverance traverse waypoints, matched by the rover site/drive in each image ID. Chosen 2026-11-14. Credit NASA/JPL-Caltech (Mastcam-Z: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU). Confidence: high for positions (same site/drive), the camera's view direction is not recorded here.
